source_text: Quidquid ad hoc genus pertinet, de isto uno posse monstrari; quoniam si semel aliquis idolis sacrificaverit, potest, donec consequatur veniam, premi impietate commissi, et manet reatus actione finita. Nullo autem pacto fieri potest ut maneat actio, et abscedebat reatus; id est, ut daemonibus sacrificare non desinat, et tamen liber a profanitate videatur
pass_a_gloss: Quidquid to this genus pertinet, about/from isto uno to-be-able monstrari; quoniam if semel someone idolis sacrificaverit, is-able, until consequatur comes, premi impietate commissi, and manet guilt actione finita. by-no however pacto to-become is-able so-that/as maneat actio, and abscedebat guilt; it is, so-that/as demon sacrificare not desinat, and nevertheless free from profanitate videatur.

lemmas.lexica: LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: Everything belonging to this class can be demonstrated by this one example. If someone has sacrificed to idols once, he can be burdened by the impiety of what he has done until he obtains forgiveness: the act has ended, but its guilt remains. But it is absolutely impossible for the act to remain and the guilt to depart—that is, for him to go on sacrificing to demons and yet be regarded as free from profanation.

choices.why: Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
